statements.subject: server
statements.description: The capability listing MUST include the atom "IMAP4rev2", but note that it doesn't have to be the first capability listed.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: Client and server implementations MUST implement the capabilities "AUTH=PLAIN" (described in [PLAIN]), and MUST implement "STARTTLS" and "LOGINDISABLED" on the cleartext port.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: An IMAP client MUST NOT issue the LOGIN command if the server advertises the LOGINDISABLED capability.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If IMAP4rev1 capability is not advertised, server responses MUST conform to this document until the client issues a command that uses an additional capability.
actions: conform server responses to IMAP4rev2 specification until client issues command using additional capability

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If both IMAP4rev1 and IMAP4rev2 capabilities are advertised, server responses MUST conform to [RFC3501] until the client issues a command that uses an additional capability.
actions: conform server responses to RFC3501 specification until client issues command using additional capability

statements.subject: imap
statements.description: Capability names SHOULD be registered with IANA using the RFC Required policy [RFC8126].

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server SHOULD NOT offer unregistered capability names.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client implementations SHOULD NOT require any capability name other than "IMAP4rev2", and possibly "STARTTLS" and "LOGINDISABLED" (on a cleartext port).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client implementations MUST ignore any unknown capability names.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY send capabilities automatically, by using the CAPABILITY response code in the initial PREAUTH or OK responses and by sending an updated CAPABILITY response code in the tagged OK response as part of a successful authentication.
actions: send CAPABILITY response code in initial PREAUTH or OK response
send updated CAPABILITY response code in tagged OK response upon successful authentication

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The list of capabilities returned by a server MAY change during the connection.
statements.trigger: STARTTLS negotiation | AUTHENTICATE command | LOGIN command
actions: update advertised capability list after successful TLS negotiation or successful authentication
